items.title: HAF Community Planning Permit
notes: Prepared By: Tanja Curic and Tristin Deveau
Ward No.: Ward 1 – Southwest, Ward 6 - Central-Columbia, Ward 7 - Uptown

David Riley, Principal, SGL Planning & Design Inc. and Justine Giancola, Partner, Dillon Consulting Limited gave a presentation outlining how the Community Planning Permit System (CPPS) works, the intent of the CPPS, and the process followed to develop the CPPS and corresponding by-law.
Tanja Curic and Tristin Deveau responded to questions of Council.
Ryan Mounsey, CEO, Urban Insights Inc. gave a presentation outlining thoughts on the CPPS and the Housing Accelerator Fund process, including the challenges that developers are facing.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Tanja Curic responded to questions of Council. David Riley, Principal, SGL Planning & Design Inc. also responded to questions of Council. Joel Cotter also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic attended the Button Factory’s Bloom & Grow Open House fundraiser on Saturday, May 9. She mentioned that it’s been a long road for the Button Factory, with the lease and accessibility upgrades, but that they and City staff have worked hard to get them where they are. The programming is taking off, there are accessible washrooms upstairs, and it’s really starting to have a community arts centre feel. They are currently fundraising for theatre space on the main floor, and the silent auction is still open.

Councillor Vasic also mentioned that the KW Water Polo Teams, the Kraken, did really great in the last few weeks. The 16U Girls team played at Nationals, May 1-3, and placed sixth overall, and second for Ontario. This past weekend, May 8-10, the 10U and 12U teams had their Provincials, and played really well. The 10U were enthusiastic and placed sixth, while the 12U Girls team received silver and the 12U Coed team received bronze.

Councillor Roe attended the Reception House Waterloo Region recognition banquet on Wednesday, May 6, in the evening. It was really fantastic to recognize community organizations and faith groups that support Reception House and the work they do, as well as the incredible contribution that newcomers make to our community.

Councillor Hanmer attended the Adventure 4 Change Celebration gala along with Councillor Roach, which was a celebration of newcomers and entrepreneurs. They talked about what started as a women’s sewing circle that’s now a thriving business operating out of St. Jacobs and their own site. It’s been great seeing the community support for the organization.

Councillor Wright mentioned that she had been to the Grand Philharmonic Choir’s fundraising event on the weekend, a walk and run in Waterloo Park. They exceeded their fundraising goal before the run/walk began, which was really encouraging.

Councillor Wright also gave a shoutout to the U14 local basketball teams, who were in Ottawa the weekend before last for Provincials. Kitchener and Waterloo faced off before the championship round, but the Waterloo Wildhawk eventually won bronze.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CORP2026-020. 2. That as part of report CORP2026-020 Council acknowledges a 2025 property-taxbase surplus of $1,259,811. 3. That Council approve $650,000 of the 2025 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Winter Control Reserve Fund to return this reserve to the Council approved minimum target level. 4. That Council approve $250,000 of the 2025 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Arts and Creative Industries Reserve as an initial contribution for this new reserve. 5. That Council approve $359,811 of the 2025 year-end property-tax base surplus be allocated to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve Fund to offset significant pressures to this reserve related to Assessment Growth shortfall. 6. That Council approve that any adjustments as a result of the year- end audit to the final surplus figure be transferred to/from the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve (TRS) (25%), Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund (CIRRF) (25%), Climate Action Reserve Fund (CARF) (25%) and the Library Expansion and Rehabilitation Reserve Fund (LXPR) (25%) in compliance with the Surplus Allocation Policy (FC-003).

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report IPPW2026-021. 2. That Council approve Zoning By-law Amendment Z-26-06 to implement the Community Planning Permit By-law, as follows: a) That Zoning By-law 2018-050 is hereby deemed to be repealed with respect to the Erb Street Corridor, as shown in Map 1, in accordance with Section 9 of O. Reg 173/16, as amended from time to time. b) That the Community Planning Permit By-law for the Erb Street Corridor be approved, as set out in Appendix ‘1’ (the “By-law”) to IPPW2026-021. 3. That Council permit City-initiated amendments to its Official Plan Amendment 58 By-law 2024-097 policies before the fifth anniversary of the first day of passing of the By-law. 4. That Council permit any person or public body authority to request an amendment to the Community Planning Permit By-law before the fifth anniversary of the first day of passing of the By-law. 5. That Council deem that any City By-law that refers to Zoning By-law 2018-050 and/or the Site Plan Control By-law 2013-124 will be taken to also mean the Community Planning Permit By-law for the Erb Street Corridor. 6. That Council approve an amendment to By-law No. 2025-080, being a by-law to Delegate Authority to Execute Documents, as set out in Appendix 2 to IPPW2026-021. 7. That Council direct staff to create a new Complete Community Contribution Reserve Fund, and to establish an accompanying policy, as part of the Reserve and Reserve Fund annual update report in December 2026.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report IPPW2026-021.

2. That Council approve Zoning By-law Amendment Z-26-06 to implement the Community Planning Permit By-law, as follows: a) That Zoning By-law 2018-050 is hereby deemed to be repealed with respect to the Erb Street Corridor, as shown in Map 1, in accordance with Section 9 of O. Reg 173/16, as amended from time to time. b) That the Community Planning Permit By-law for the Erb Street Corridor be approved, as set out in Appendix ‘1’ (the “By-law”) to IPPW2026-021.

3. That Council permit City-initiated amendments to its Official Plan Amendment 58 By-law 2024-097 policies before the fifth anniversary of the first day of passing of the By-law.

4. That Council permit any person or public body authority to request an amendment to the Community Planning Permit By-law before the fifth anniversary of the first day of passing of the By-law.

5. That Council deem that any City By-law that refers to Zoning By-law 2018-050 and/or the Site Plan Control By-law 2013-124 will be taken to also mean the Community Planning Permit By-law for the Erb Street Corridor.

6. That Council approve an amendment to By-law No. 2025-080, being a by-law to Delegate Authority to Execute Documents, as set out in Appendix 2 to IPPW2026-021.

7. That Council direct staff to create a new Complete Community Contribution Reserve Fund, and to establish an accompanying policy, as part of the Reserve and Reserve Fund annual update report in December 2026.
